Subject: Renewal: EU onshore + APAC burst standby — proposed SOW & pricing

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our discussion, attached is a draft SOW that adds EU onshore data residency (single-tenant node in Frankfurt), an APAC warm-standby entitlement for surge capacity, and a 12-month renewal with a stepped SKU uplift (10% uplift in committed units for months 1–3, then baseline).

Key highlights in the SOW:
- EU onshore: dedicated tenant, SOC2-compliant audit trail, KMS integration for customer-managed keys.
- APAC warm-standby: cold standby replications + manual failover window; optional automated failover available in the premium SLA.
- Pricing: see pricing matrix (attached) — I included two options (standard renewal uplift vs. committed uplift with burst credits).
- Ops handoff: we propose a two-week cutoff for the migration window and a runbook handover (link in the Drive).

Could you confirm (a) whether the procurement team needs any additional security artifacts, and (b) if the committed uplift option is of interest? If so, I'll schedule a joint call with our ops lead to walk through the runbook and the failover procedures.

Attachments: CW_SOW_EU_Onshore_v1.pdf; CW_pricing_matrix_q4_2025.xlsx; residency_runbook_link.txt

Best,

Hi Elena / Liam —

Thanks for the questions — quick responses inline below and attaching the SOC2 excerpt + KMS FAQ.

Responses:
- SOC2 / KMS: We have an SOC2 Type II report covering the EU tenant controls and a separate KMS integration guide. Attaching the SOC2 excerpt (redacted) and the KMS integration FAQ. No additional paperwork required beyond standard MSA/KMS key exchange forms; Kimberly, feel free to flag if we should require anything extra.
- Failover / cache warm-up: For the model family they run, expect a cache cold-start impact of ~45–120s for large context ops on first failover; p95 latency typically increases by ~25–40% during the priming window. Our runbook recommends an orchestration step to pre-warm the most common prefixes; we can outline a test plan during the tech ramp.
- Burst credits: Credits are consumed first-in, first-out against overages; unused burst credits do not roll automatically but we can add a 30-day grace window in the committed uplift addendum if Procurement needs it.

Next steps I propose:
1) Technical ramp: 30–45m with Marissa + Liam + ClearWave SREs next week to walk the runbook and one simulated failover test.
2) Procurement: Kimberly will provide the minimal redlines for the KMS and residency clauses; once accepted we can issue final SOW and DocuSign link.
3) Commercial: If ClearWave picks the committed-uplift SKU we’ll apply the 10% onboarding credit and provide a one-time burst credit pool as previously discussed.

Proposed times for tech ramp: Tue 2025-12-09 09:00–09:45 PST or Wed 2025-12-10 16:00–16:45 PST. Please confirm availability and I’ll calendar and send meeting materials.
